content:
ana_marketing: Quick sync — we need an updated battlecard + webinar narrative that clearly positions us vs cloud AI platforms, LLM APIs, and infra vendors. Primary theme: 'Serving-first economics' (latency predictability, unit cost transparency, graceful fallbacks). Asks: 1) single-page bullets for SDRs, 2) short benchmark summary for webinar slides, 3) procurement objection handlers. Deadline: EOD Thu. Who can own?

mike_sales: I can own the SDR one-pager. Will need 3-4 sharp soundbites and 2 quick rebuttals for pricing vs reserved capacity.

sarah_pm: I'll draft the benchmark narrative + the explanatory note on what the numbers mean (sequence length, burstiness). Want the benchmark to emphasize p95 latency SLO and cost-per-conversation, not raw throughput.

jen_content: I can do the copy for the one-pager and a short slide intro. Can someone paste the latest bench numbers? Also want a 1-sentence hero claim for the webinar landing.

tina_research: Pasted rough bench nuggets below — these are from staging workload 2026-03/serving-run-4. Caveat: not public yet, tighten before publish.

```text
Workload: multi-turn chat, avg seq len 400 tokens
Redwood Inference (quantized profile): p50 40ms, p95 120ms, cost-per-convo $0.018
CloudX-managed endpoint (same model size): p50 80ms, p95 240ms, cost-per-convo $0.04
InfraVendor (self-hosted baseline): p50 30ms, p95 300ms (under burst), cost-per-convo $0.03
```

ana_marketing: Nice — Tina, can you add a 1-line on test conditions we can paste on the slide (region, instance type, concurrency)? We should avoid absolute claims; use relative phrasing: "~2x lower p95 latency vs CloudX in our tests".

mike_sales: For procurement/IT objections: they ask about compliance and E2E control. We should have a short script: "Dedicated or Private deployments with KMS/HSM options and audit logs — same control surface as on-prem with cloud-level uptime." Also need a cost-savings math example for reserved vs on-demand.

jen_content: Draft hero sentence for landing: "Serve LLMs predictably — lower latency, clearer unit economics, and built-in fallbacks that keep apps online." Thoughts? :thinking_face:

sarah_pm: Love the hero. Maybe tighten: "Predictable LLM inference — lower p95 latency, transparent unit costs, and automatic fallbacks."

ana_marketing: Both good; pick one in final. Also need 3 quick battlecard bullets vs each competitor bucket (cloud APIs, managed endpoints, infra vendors). I'll sketch and y'all edit.

ana_marketing: Draft bullets (please edit inline):
- Vs Cloud APIs: predictable p95 latency, explicit fallback tiers, and cost-to-quality controls for production apps.
- Vs Managed Endpoints: per-token economics + batching/kv-cache optimizations that reduce unit cost by design.
- Vs Self-hosted Infra: unified control plane + rollouts, less ops overhead, and SLA-backed dedicated pools.

jen_content: Edits: make them snappier and add a one-liner objection handler under each. Example:
- Vs Cloud APIs — Bullet: "Latency & economics you can rely on"; Objection handler: "We provide SLAs and burst capacity paths plus a transparent cost breakdown to model your guesstimates."
- Vs Managed Endpoints — Bullet: "Optimized serving primitives (caching, batching, quantized profiles)"; Handler: "We ship recommended configs and automated suggestions — not just a dumb endpoint."
- Vs Infra Vendors — Bullet: "Same API across hosted/dedicated/private"; Handler: "You get enterprise controls without rewriting your infra stack."

tina_research: Quick note for the benchmark slide text (short): "Testbed: eu-west-1, A100-equivalent nodes, steady-state 80% util, 1k concurrent sessions simulated. See appendix for raw logs."

ops_bot: deploy-notify: benchmark artifacts uploaded: https://storage.redwood.example/bench/serving-run-4/artifacts.tar.gz

mike_sales: Can someone put together a tiny pricing example: 1M convs/month, show per-convo cost and 3-tier cost diff (hosted on-demand, dedicated reserved, private)? I'll convert to an ROI slide.

ana_marketing: Sarah + Tina, please finalize benchmark text and a single slide with the table and one chart by tomorrow morning. Jen, mike — finalize copy and SDR one-pager. I'll assemble the battlecard and sample slide deck, then we'll do a quick dry-run on Wed.

jen_content: On it. I'll push a draft to this doc: https://docs.google.com/document/draft-battlecard-70321 (placeholder) — will tag when ready.

sarah_pm: ETA for slide draft: tomorrow 10am PT.

tina_research: I'll produce a sanitized bench table (no raw IP) by EOD today.

mike_sales: I'll mock the procurement script + ROI numbers and post here by 5pm.

ana_marketing: Great. Final ask: keep all claims defensible — label anything "internal" or "customer-facing" explicitly. Use relative phrasing where possible ("~2x lower p95 in our tests"). :thumbsup:

jen_content: :thumbsup: will do.

ana_marketing: Thanks team — marking owners on the thread so it's clear. We'll sync 10min before the Wed dry-run.

(END)
